learn.title: Same shape, same size
learn.body: Two figures are congruent if one can be moved onto the other exactly. Their matching sides are equal and their matching angles are equal. When we say triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $DEF$, the order of the letters shows which parts match.

learn.title: Three shortcuts
learn.body: You do not need all six matches to prove triangles congruent. SSS: all three sides match. SAS: two sides and the angle between them match. ASA: two angles and the side between them match.

learn.title: What does not work
learn.body: AAA does not work: triangles with equal angles can be different sizes. SSA, two sides and an angle that is not between them, is also not enough. Always check where the angle sits relative to the sides.

learn.title: Use SSS and SAS
learn.body: Check whether the triangles are congruent.
steps: Triangle 1 has sides $3,4,5$. Triangle 2 has sides $5,3,4$.
All three sides match, so the triangles are congruent by SSS.
Two triangles each have sides 6 and 8 with a $50^\circ$ angle between them.
That is SAS, so they are congruent, and the third sides are equal.

learn.body: Once triangles are congruent, every matching part is equal. That is how you prove a side or an angle is equal.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT enough to prove two triangles congruent?
questions.explanation: Equal angles only tell you the shapes match, not the sizes. SSS, SAS and ASA fix the triangle exactly.

questions.prompt: Two triangles have two pairs of equal sides and equal angles between them. Which rule applies?
questions.explanation: Two sides and the angle between them is SAS.

questions.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ is congruent to triangle $DEF$, and $AB=7$. How long is $DE$?
questions.explanation: $A$ matches $D$ and $B$ matches $E$, so side $AB$ matches side $DE$.

questions.prompt: Two triangles have two equal angles and the equal side between them. Which rule applies?
questions.explanation: Two angles with the side between them is ASA.

questions.prompt: In congruent triangles, matching parts are \_\_.
questions.explanation: Congruent means identical in size and shape, so every matching side and angle are equal.

questions.prompt: Two triangles share two sides, and the equal angle is NOT between those sides. What can you say?
choices: It is not enough to prove congruence
questions.explanation: That is SSA, which can fit two different triangles, so it does not prove congruence.

questions.prompt: Match each rule to what must match.
pairs: Two sides and the angle between
Two angles and the side between
questions.explanation: The rule name lists the parts in the order they appear around the triangle.
